class="row"><div class="col-md-6 col-lg-8"><p> Correlations between genotype and tissue-specific gene expression levels will help identify regions of the genome that influence whether and how much a gene is expressed. GTEx will help researchers to understand inherited susceptibility to disease and will be a resource database and tissue bank for many studies in the future. </p><p> The Genotype-Tissue Expression (GTEx) project aims to provide to the scientific community a resource with which to study human gene expression and regulation and its relationship to genetic variation. This project will collect and analyze multiple human tissues from donors who are also densely genotyped, to assess genetic variation within their genomes. By analyzing global RNA expression within individual tissues and treating the expression levels of genes as quantitative traits, variations in gene expression that are highly correlated with genetic variation can be identified as expression quantitative trait loci, or eQTLs. </p><p> Despite the rapid progress achieved using genome-wide association studies (GWAS; See: <a href="http://www.genome.gov/26525384" target="_blank">http://www.genome.gov/26525384 <i class="fas fa-external-link-alt"></i></a>) to identify genetic changes associated with common human diseases, such as heart disease, cancer, diabetes, asthma, and stroke, a large majority of these genetic changes lies outside of the protein-coding regions of genes and often even outside of the genes themselves, making it difficult to discern which genes are affected and by what mechanism. The comprehensive identification of human eQTLs will greatly help to identify genes whose expression is affected by genetic variation, and will provide a valuable basis on which to study the mechanism of that gene regulation. </p><p> The project will also involve consultation and research into the ethical, legal and social issues raised by the research, support for statistical methods development, and creation of a database to house existing and  <a href="http://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/gtex/test/GTEX2/gtex.cgi" target="_blank">GTEx-generated eQTL data <i class="fas fa-external-link-alt"></i></a>. The database will allow users to view and download computed eQTL results and provide a controlled access system for de-identified individual-level genotype, expression, and clinical data. The associated tissue repository will also serve as a resource for many additional kinds of analyses. </p></div><div class="col-md-6 col-lg-4"><img alt="A diagram of the GTEx project" src="'+Os+'" width="90%"></div></div></div><hr>',2)),(0,s.createElementVNode)("div",Js,[a[1]||(a[1]=(0,s.createElementVNode)("h3",null,"Frequently Asked Questions",-1)),(0,s.createVNode)(i,{to:"/faq"},{default:(0,s.withCtx)((()=>a[0]||(a[0]=[(0,s.createTextVNode)(" Go to GTEx FAQs Site "),(0,s.createElementVNode)("i",{class:"fas"},null,-1)])),void 0,!0),_:1})]),a[15]||(a[15]=(0,s.createElementVNode)("hr",null,null,-1)),a[16]||(a[16]=(0,s.createElementVNode)("div",{id:"staticTextConsortium"},[(0,s.createElementVNode)("h3",null,"The GTEx Consortium"),(0,s.createElementVNode)("h4",null,"GTEx Consortium Members"),(0,s.createElementVNode)("ul",null,[(0,s.createElementVNode)("li",null,[(0,s.createElementVNode)("a",{href:"https://storage.googleapis.com/gtex-public-data/GTEx_Consortium_Member_List_May_2017.pdf",target:"_blank"}," GTEx Consortium Membership as of May 2017 - download as PDF ")])])],-1)),a[17]||(a[17]=(0,s.createElementVNode)("hr",null,null,-1)),(0,s.createElementVNode)("div",_s,[a[12]||(a[12]=(0,s.createElementVNode)("h3",null,"GTEx Data Release and Publication Policy",-1)),(0,s.createElementVNode)("div",$s,[(0,s.createElementVNode)("div",en,[a[11]||(a[11]=(0,s.createElementVNode)("div",{class:"panel-heading"},[(0,s.createElementVNode)("h4",{class:"panel-title"},[(0,s.createElementVNode)("a",{"data-toggle":"collapse",href:"#policy","data-parent":"#policyPanel"}," GTEx Data Release and Publication Policy (v05-08-15;
